The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar (1), so pray to your Lord and sacrifice (2). Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off (3).﴾

.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿al-Kawthar﴾. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of al-Kawthar. Some of them said: It is a river in Paradise which Allah gave to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold and silver, flowing over pearls and rubies. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Muharib ibn Dithar al-Bahili, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river in Paradise whose banks are gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its water whiter than snow, sweeter than honey, and its soil more fragrant than the scent of musk."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold and silver, flowing over rubies and pearls, its water whiter than snow and sweeter than honey."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyya, from Shaqiq or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'isha: "O Mother of the Believers, what is Buttan al-Jannah?" She said: "The middle of Paradise. Its banks are palaces of pearls and rubies, its soil is musk, and its pebbles are pearls and rubies."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Nadr and Shababa narrated to us, both said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from a man, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise; no one puts his two fingers in his ears except that he hears the murmur of that river."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far; and Ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Anas, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, of hollow pearls."

⁕ Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, upon which are vessels equal in number to the stars of the sky."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever wishes to hear the murmur of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "A river in Paradise, whose two banks are of hollow pearls."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Mu'adh 'Isa ibn Yazid, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in the buttan (inner part) of Paradise, the middle of Paradise. In it is a river whose banks are hollow pearls, and in it are vessels for the people of Paradise equal in number to the stars of the sky."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river which Allah gave Muhammad (ﷺ) in Paradise."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Mas'ada narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its soil is pungent musk, and its water is wine."

⁕ Ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river in Paradise."

⁕ al-Rabi' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Shurayk ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrate to us, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, Jibril took him into the lowest heaven. There he came upon a river, upon which was a palace of pearls and zabarjad (chrysolite). He went to smell its soil, and it was musk. He said: 'O Jibril, what is this river?' He said: 'It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept hidden for you.'"

And others said: What is meant by al-Kawthar is abundant good.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, he said: Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding al-Kawthar: "It is the abundant good which Allah gave him." Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Indeed, people claim that it is a river in Paradise." He said: Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is part of the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who said: Muharib ibn Dithar said: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: It is abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth, by Allah."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is the abundant good which Allah gave." I said to Sa'id: "We used to hear that it is a river in Paradise." He said: "It is the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Imara ibn Abi Hafsa, from 'Ikrima, who said: "It is prophethood and the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Harmi ibn 'Imara narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, he said: 'Imara informed me, from 'Ikrima, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good, the Qur'an and wisdom."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, he said: 'Imara ibn Abi Hafsa narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, that he said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hilal, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and he said: "Allah multiplied good for him." I said: "A river in Paradise?" He said: "A river and other things."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Mujahid: "Al-Kawthar: all good."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The good of this world and the Hereafter."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding al-Kawthar, who said: "It is abundant good."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Badr ibn 'Uthman, who heard 'Ikrima say regarding al-Kawthar: "What was given to the Prophet of good, prophethood and the Qur'an."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Badr, from 'Ikrima, his saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "The good which Allah gave: prophethood and Islam."

And others said: It is a pool (hawd) given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mutar, from 'Ata': ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A pool in Paradise given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Mutar narrated to us, he said: I asked 'Ata' while we were circumambulating the House, about His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and he said: "A pool given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

The most correct of these views in my judgment is the view of the one who said: It is the name of the river which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given in Paradise, and Allah described it as abundant because of its great rank.

We only said that this is the most correct of these views because of the successive reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it is so.

Mention of the reports transmitted regarding that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrate from Qatada, from Anas, who said: "When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was taken up into Paradise, or as he said, there appeared to him a river whose banks are hollow rubies, or he said: hollow (mujawwab). The angel with him struck it with his hand, and drew out musk. Muhammad said to the angel with him: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.' He said: 'The Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and he saw at it a great trace.'" Or as he said.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While I was walking in Paradise, there appeared to me a river whose banks are domes of hollow pearls. The angel with me said: 'Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.' He struck his hand toward its ground and drew out musk from its clay."

⁕ Ibn 'Awf narrated to me, he said: Adam narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I was taken up to the heaven, I came upon a river whose banks are domes of hollow pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which your Lord gave you.' The angel then swung his hand and drew out its clay as very fragrant musk."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise, and there I was with a river whose banks are tents of pearls. I struck my hand into what flowed in it, and it was very fragrant musk. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, he said: Hammam narrated to us, he said: Qatada narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar to the report of Yazid from Sa'id.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Ayyub al-'Abbas narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to us, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river which Allah gave me in Paradise. Its soil is white musk, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Birds whose necks are like the necks of camels come to drink from it." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed they are delicious (lush)?" He said: "Whoever eats them is more delighted than they are."

⁕ Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqama ibn Abi Waqqas al-Laythi informed us, from Kathir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise when I was taken up, and I was given al-Kawthar. It is a river in Paradise whose two sides are hollow houses of pearls."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, he said: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas: that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Kawthar?" He said: "A river which Allah gave me in Paradise. It is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed they are delicious (lush)." He said: "Whoever eats them is more delighted than they are."

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to me, from Ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he mentioned the like.

⁕ 'Umar ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri narrated to us, that his brother 'Abd Allah informed him that Anas ibn Malik, companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him: that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "What is al-Kawthar?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A river which Allah gave me in Paradise. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "Indeed they are delicious (lush), O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Whoever eats them is more delighted than they are."

'Umar ibn 'Uthman said: Ibn Abi Uways narrated, and my father narrated to me, from the nephew of al-Zuhri, from his father, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding al-Kawthar, the like of this.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' narrated to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold, its course over ruby and pearl, its soil more fragrant than musk, its water sweeter than honey and whiter than snow."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, he said: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "Tell us from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth, by Allah; it is indeed abundant good. But tell us from Ibn 'Umar, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise whose banks are of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies.'"

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw a river whose banks are pearls. I said: 'O Jibril, what is this?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, he said: Hizam ibn 'Uthman informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Usama ibn Zayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came one day to Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and did not find him. He asked his wife about him, and she was from the Banu al-Najjar. She said: "He went out, may my father be your ransom, just now, heading toward you. I think he missed you in some alleys of the Banu al-Najjar. Will you not enter, O Messenger of Allah?" He entered, and she offered him hays (a date-and-butter dish), and he ate from it. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, may it be pleasant and wholesome for you. You came, and I was about to come to you to congratulate you and give you glad tidings. Abu 'Umara informed me that you were given a river in Paradise called al-Kawthar." He said: "Indeed, and its land (ardh) is ruby, coral, chrysolite, and pearl."

* *

And His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the prayer which Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to perform by this address, and the meaning of His saying: ﴿and sacrifice﴾. Some of them said: It urges him to be steadfast in the obligatory prayer and to guard its times, by His saying: ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Tufawi narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad ibn Abi al-Ja'd narrated to me, from 'Asim al-Jahduri, from 'Uqba ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: "Placing the right hand upon the left in prayer."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Jahduri, from 'Uqba ibn Dhabyan, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: "Placing the hand upon the hand in prayer."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Asim al-Jahduri, from 'Uqba ibn Zuhayr, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: "He placed his right hand upon the middle of his left forearm, then placed both upon his chest."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, from al-Shaʿbi, the like of it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from ʿAsim al-Jahdari, from ʿUqbah ibn Zuhayr, from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: placing the right hand upon the left during the prayer.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Abu al-Qumus, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: placing the hand upon the hand during the prayer.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih al-Khurasani narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from ʿAsim al-Jahdari, from his father, from ʿUqbah ibn Zabyan, that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning the saying of Allah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: he placed his right hand on the middle of his left forearm, then placed them both on his chest.

Others said: Rather, by His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ is meant the obligatory prayer, and by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ is meant that one raises his hands to the throat at the beginning of the prayer and when entering into it.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: the prayer, and "sacrifice": by raising his hands at the first takbir at the opening.

Others said: By His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ is meant the obligatory prayer, and by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾: the sacrifice of camels.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm and Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the obligatory prayer, and the sacrifice of camels.

⁕ Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Hajjaj, that they both said concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: the dawn prayer at Muzdalifah, and the sacrifice of camels at Mina.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Qatr, from ʿAta': ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the dawn prayer, and sacrifice the camels. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the obligatory prayer, and the sacrifice (al-nahr): the offering (nusk) and slaughter on the day of al-Adha.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the dawn prayer.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is: pray on the day of sacrifice the prayer of the festival, and sacrifice your offering.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Jabir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to sacrifice before he prayed, so he was commanded to pray and then sacrifice.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from ʿIkrimah: pray the prayer and sacrifice the offering (nusk).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from Abu Ja'far, ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾, he said: the prayer; and ʿIkrimah said: the prayer and the sacrifice of the offering.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: when you pray on the day of al-Adha, then sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Qatr narrated to us, saying: I asked ʿAta' about His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: you pray and you sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: slaughter.

⁕ He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Aban ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the slaughter.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the sacrifice of camels, and the prayer on the day of sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the prayer of al-Adha, and the sacrifice: the sacrifice of camels.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the places of sacrifice of camels at Mina.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from ʿIkrimah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the sacrifice of the offering.

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he says: slaughter on the day of sacrifice.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the sacrifice of camels.

Others said: This was said to the Prophet ﷺ because some people used to pray to other than Allah and sacrifice to other than Him, so it was said to him: make your prayer and your sacrifice for Allah, since whoever disbelieves in Allah directs it to another.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he says: Indeed, people used to pray to other than Allah and sacrifice to other than Allah; so when We have granted you al-Kawthar, O Muhammad, let your prayer and your sacrifice be for none but Me.

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the Prophet ﷺ and his companions were besieged and were prevented from the House, so Allah commanded him to pray and sacrifice the camels, and to depart, and he did so.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah al-Bajali narrated to me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, that he said: This verse, meaning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, was on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: Sacrifice and return. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, delivered the sermon of the Fitr and the sacrifice [[Report 190: This, like report 183, is broken (munqati') between Ibn Jurayj and Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Kathir (1:53) and al-Suyuti (1:16) also transmitted it, but in it "Ibn Humayd" occurs instead of "Ibn Jarir".]], then prayed two rakʿahs, then departed to the camels and sacrificed them. That is when He says: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: pray, and call upon your Lord and ask Him.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: pray to your Lord and ask.

It was the practice of some scholars of Arabic to interpret His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ as: face the qiblah with your throat. It is reported that he heard some Arabs say: "Their dwellings face one another (tatanahar)," meaning: this one is opposite that one, i.e., in front of it. It is also mentioned that some of Banu Asad recited to him:

Abu Hakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujalid,
and the lord of the people of al-Abtah, the one who faces (al-mutanahir)?

[[Report 191: Ibn Kathir also transmitted this (1:53).]]

I.e., one whose throat faces another's throat.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is the view of the one who said: the meaning is: make all your prayer purely for your Lord, to the exclusion of whatever else, of rivals and gods; and likewise make your sacrifice for Him, not for idols, in gratitude to Him for the honour and the good which He has granted you, which has no equal, and which He has singled you out with, namely His giving you al-Kawthar.

I say that this is the most correct of the opinions on this matter because Allah, mighty is His praise, informed His Prophet ﷺ of the honour and dignity with which He had favoured him, and of His bounty upon him in giving him al-Kawthar, and then followed that with His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾. It was thus known that He singled him out for prayer to Him and sacrifice as thanks to Him, for the blessing He had made him aware of in giving him al-Kawthar. There is no basis for restricting part of the prayer, or part of the sacrifice, to this matter, since it is an exhortation to give thanks for blessings.

The meaning of the speech, then, is: Indeed, We have granted you, O Muhammad, al-Kawthar, as a favour from Us upon you and an honour from Us to you. So devote your worship sincerely to your Lord, and single out for Him your prayer and your sacrifice, in contrast to what the one who disbelieves in Him does, who worships other than Him and sacrifices to idols.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾

By His saying, mighty is His praise: ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾ means: indeed, your hater, O Muhammad, and your foe, ﴿is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾. By "al-abtar" is meant: the least and most humiliated, the one whose line is cut off, who has no offspring.

The exegetes differed concerning who is meant by this. Some said: it refers to al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he says: your enemy.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: it is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, who said: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr say: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: it is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hilal, who said: I asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr about His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: your enemy, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, was cut off from his people.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, who said: I am a hater of Muhammad, and whoever is hated by people is the one cut off.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: it is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, who said: I am a hater of Muhammad, and he is cut off, having no offspring. Allah said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. Qatadah said: al-abtar: the lowly, the insignificant, the humiliated.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾: this is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; it has reached us that he said: I am a hater of Muhammad.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: the man would say: Muhammad is only cut off, he has no offspring as you see, and Allah said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾.

Others said: it refers to ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shimr ibn ʿAtiyyah, who said: ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt used to say: he (the Prophet ﷺ) will have no surviving son, and he is cut off; so Allah revealed these verses concerning him: ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾, ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, ﴿is the one cut off﴾.

Others said: it refers to a group of Quraysh.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, concerning this verse: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in jibt and taghut and say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way"?﴾ He said: it was revealed concerning Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, who came to Mecca, and its people said to him: are we better, or this cut-off one (al-sunbur) cut off from his people? We are the people of pilgrimage, and with us is the place of sacrifice of camels. He said: you are better. So Allah revealed this verse concerning him, and revealed concerning those who said to the Prophet ﷺ what they said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. [[Report 192: This chain has passed as report 185. The text of the report is in Ibn Kathir (1:53), who said after these narrations: "The tafsir previously transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas is more general and comprehensive", meaning report 188.]]

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Badr ibn ʿUthman, from ʿIkrimah ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ, Quraysh said: Muhammad has been cut off from us, so it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. He said: the one who calls you cut off is the one cut off.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf came to Mecca, they came to him and said: We are the people of watering and the keeping of the Kaaba, and you are the chief of the people of Medina; are we better, or this cut-off sunbur from his people, who claims he is better than us? He said: rather, you are better than him. So this was revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. He said: and this was revealed to him: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book﴾ ... to His saying ﴿a helper﴾.

The most correct of these views in my opinion is to say: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that the hater of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the least and most humiliated, whose line is cut off. This is the description of everyone among mankind who hates him, even if the verse was revealed concerning a particular individual.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar (1), so pray to your Lord and sacrifice (2). Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off (3).﴾

.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿al-Kawthar﴾. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of al-Kawthar. Some of them said: It is a river in Paradise which Allah gave to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold and silver, flowing over pearls and rubies. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Muharib ibn Dithar al-Bahili, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river in Paradise whose banks are gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its water whiter than snow, sweeter than honey, and its soil more fragrant than the scent of musk."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold and silver, flowing over rubies and pearls, its water whiter than snow and sweeter than honey."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyya, from Shaqiq or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'isha: "O Mother of the Believers, what is Buttan al-Jannah?" She said: "The middle of Paradise. Its banks are palaces of pearls and rubies, its soil is musk, and its pebbles are pearls and rubies."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Nadr and Shababa narrated to us, both said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from a man, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise; no one puts his two fingers in his ears except that he hears the murmur of that river."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far; and Ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Anas, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, of hollow pearls."

⁕ Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, upon which are vessels equal in number to the stars of the sky."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever wishes to hear the murmur of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "A river in Paradise, whose two banks are of hollow pearls."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Mu'adh 'Isa ibn Yazid, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in the buttan (inner part) of Paradise, the middle of Paradise. In it is a river whose banks are hollow pearls, and in it are vessels for the people of Paradise equal in number to the stars of the sky."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river which Allah gave Muhammad (ﷺ) in Paradise."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Mas'ada narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its soil is pungent musk, and its water is wine."

⁕ Ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river in Paradise."

⁕ al-Rabi' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Shurayk ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrate to us, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, Jibril took him into the lowest heaven. There he came upon a river, upon which was a palace of pearls and zabarjad (chrysolite). He went to smell its soil, and it was musk. He said: 'O Jibril, what is this river?' He said: 'It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept hidden for you.'"

And others said: What is meant by al-Kawthar is abundant good.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, he said: Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding al-Kawthar: "It is the abundant good which Allah gave him." Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Indeed, people claim that it is a river in Paradise." He said: Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is part of the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who said: Muharib ibn Dithar said: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: It is abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth, by Allah."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is the abundant good which Allah gave." I said to Sa'id: "We used to hear that it is a river in Paradise." He said: "It is the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Imara ibn Abi Hafsa, from 'Ikrima, who said: "It is prophethood and the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Harmi ibn 'Imara narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, he said: 'Imara informed me, from 'Ikrima, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good, the Qur'an and wisdom."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, he said: 'Imara ibn Abi Hafsa narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, that he said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hilal, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and he said: "Allah multiplied good for him." I said: "A river in Paradise?" He said: "A river and other things."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Mujahid: "Al-Kawthar: all good."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The good of this world and the Hereafter."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding al-Kawthar, who said: "It is abundant good."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Badr ibn 'Uthman, who heard 'Ikrima say regarding al-Kawthar: "What was given to the Prophet of good, prophethood and the Qur'an."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Badr, from 'Ikrima, his saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "The good which Allah gave: prophethood and Islam."

And others said: It is a pool (hawd) given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mutar, from 'Ata': ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A pool in Paradise given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Mutar narrated to us, he said: I asked 'Ata' while we were circumambulating the House, about His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and he said: "A pool given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

The most correct of these views in my judgment is the view of the one who said: It is the name of the river which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given in Paradise, and Allah described it as abundant because of its great rank.

We only said that this is the most correct of these views because of the successive reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it is so.

Mention of the reports transmitted regarding that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrate from Qatada, from Anas, who said: "When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was taken up into Paradise, or as he said, there appeared to him a river whose banks are hollow rubies, or he said: hollow (mujawwab). The angel with him struck it with his hand, and drew out musk. Muhammad said to the angel with him: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.' He said: 'The Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and he saw at it a great trace.'" Or as he said.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While I was walking in Paradise, there appeared to me a river whose banks are domes of hollow pearls. The angel with me said: 'Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.' He struck his hand toward its ground and drew out musk from its clay."

⁕ Ibn 'Awf narrated to me, he said: Adam narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I was taken up to the heaven, I came upon a river whose banks are domes of hollow pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which your Lord gave you.' The angel then swung his hand and drew out its clay as very fragrant musk."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise, and there I was with a river whose banks are tents of pearls. I struck my hand into what flowed in it, and it was very fragrant musk. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, he said: Hammam narrated to us, he said: Qatada narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar to the report of Yazid from Sa'id.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Ayyub al-'Abbas narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, narrated to us, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river which Allah gave me in Paradise. Its soil is white musk, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Birds whose necks are like the necks of camels come to drink from it." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed they are delicious (lush)?" He said: "Whoever eats them is more delighted than they are."

⁕ Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqama ibn Abi Waqqas al-Laythi informed us, from Kathir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise when I was taken up, and I was given al-Kawthar. It is a river in Paradise whose two sides are hollow houses of pearls."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, he said: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas: that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Kawthar?" He said: "A river which Allah gave me in Paradise. It is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed they are delicious (lush)." He said: "Whoever eats them is more delighted than they are."

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to me, from Ibn al-Hadi, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he mentioned the like.

⁕ 'Umar ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri narrated to us, that his brother 'Abd Allah informed him that Anas ibn Malik, companion of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him: that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "What is al-Kawthar?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A river which Allah gave me in Paradise. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: "Indeed they are delicious (lush), O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Whoever eats them is more delighted than they are."

'Umar ibn 'Uthman said: Ibn Abi Uways narrated, and my father narrated to me, from the nephew of al-Zuhri, from his father, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding al-Kawthar, the like of this.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' narrated to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold, its course over ruby and pearl, its soil more fragrant than musk, its water sweeter than honey and whiter than snow."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, he said: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "Tell us from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth, by Allah; it is indeed abundant good. But tell us from Ibn 'Umar, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise whose banks are of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies.'"

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw a river whose banks are pearls. I said: 'O Jibril, what is this?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, he said: Hizam ibn 'Uthman informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Usama ibn Zayd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came one day to Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and did not find him. He asked his wife about him, and she was from the Banu al-Najjar. She said: "He went out, may my father be your ransom, just now, heading toward you. I think he missed you in some alleys of the Banu al-Najjar. Will you not enter, O Messenger of Allah?" He entered, and she offered him hays (a date-and-butter dish), and he ate from it. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, may it be pleasant and wholesome for you. You came, and I was about to come to you to congratulate you and give you glad tidings. Abu 'Umara informed me that you were given a river in Paradise called al-Kawthar." He said: "Indeed, and its land (ardh) is ruby, coral, chrysolite, and pearl."

* *

And His saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the prayer which Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to perform by this address, and the meaning of His saying: ﴿and sacrifice﴾. Some of them said: It urges him to be steadfast in the obligatory prayer and to guard its times, by His saying: ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Tufawi narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad ibn Abi al-Ja'd narrated to me, from 'Asim al-Jahduri, from 'Uqba ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: "Placing the right hand upon the left in prayer."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Jahduri, from 'Uqba ibn Dhabyan, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: "Placing the hand upon the hand in prayer."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Asim al-Jahduri, from 'Uqba ibn Zuhayr, from his father, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, ﴿so pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: "He placed his right hand upon the middle of his left forearm, then placed both upon his chest."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, from al-Shaʿbi, the like of it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from ʿAsim al-Jahdari, from ʿUqbah ibn Zuhayr, from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: placing the right hand upon the left during the prayer.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Abu al-Qumus, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: placing the hand upon the hand during the prayer.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih al-Khurasani narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from ʿAsim al-Jahdari, from his father, from ʿUqbah ibn Zabyan, that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning the saying of Allah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: he placed his right hand on the middle of his left forearm, then placed them both on his chest.

Others said: Rather, by His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ is meant the obligatory prayer, and by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ is meant that one raises his hands to the throat at the beginning of the prayer and when entering into it.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: the prayer, and "sacrifice": by raising his hands at the first takbir at the opening.

Others said: By His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾ is meant the obligatory prayer, and by His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾: the sacrifice of camels.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm and Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the obligatory prayer, and the sacrifice of camels.

⁕ Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Hajjaj, that they both said concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾: the dawn prayer at Muzdalifah, and the sacrifice of camels at Mina.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Qatr, from ʿAta': ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the dawn prayer, and sacrifice the camels. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the obligatory prayer, and the sacrifice (al-nahr): the offering (nusk) and slaughter on the day of al-Adha.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the dawn prayer.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is: pray on the day of sacrifice the prayer of the festival, and sacrifice your offering.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Jabir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to sacrifice before he prayed, so he was commanded to pray and then sacrifice.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from ʿIkrimah: pray the prayer and sacrifice the offering (nusk).

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from Abu Ja'far, ﴿So pray to your Lord﴾, he said: the prayer; and ʿIkrimah said: the prayer and the sacrifice of the offering.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: when you pray on the day of al-Adha, then sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Qatr narrated to us, saying: I asked ʿAta' about His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: you pray and you sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: slaughter.

⁕ He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Aban ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the slaughter.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the sacrifice of camels, and the prayer on the day of sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the prayer of al-Adha, and the sacrifice: the sacrifice of camels.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the places of sacrifice of camels at Mina.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from ʿIkrimah ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the sacrifice of the offering.

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he says: slaughter on the day of sacrifice.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: the sacrifice of camels.

Others said: This was said to the Prophet ﷺ because some people used to pray to other than Allah and sacrifice to other than Him, so it was said to him: make your prayer and your sacrifice for Allah, since whoever disbelieves in Allah directs it to another.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he says: Indeed, people used to pray to other than Allah and sacrifice to other than Allah; so when We have granted you al-Kawthar, O Muhammad, let your prayer and your sacrifice be for none but Me.

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the Prophet ﷺ and his companions were besieged and were prevented from the House, so Allah commanded him to pray and sacrifice the camels, and to depart, and he did so.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah al-Bajali narrated to me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, that he said: This verse, meaning His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, was on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said: Sacrifice and return. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood, delivered the sermon of the Fitr and the sacrifice [[Report 190: This, like report 183, is broken (munqati') between Ibn Jurayj and Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Kathir (1:53) and al-Suyuti (1:16) also transmitted it, but in it "Ibn Humayd" occurs instead of "Ibn Jarir".]], then prayed two rakʿahs, then departed to the camels and sacrificed them. That is when He says: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: pray, and call upon your Lord and ask Him.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, he said: pray to your Lord and ask.

It was the practice of some scholars of Arabic to interpret His saying ﴿and sacrifice﴾ as: face the qiblah with your throat. It is reported that he heard some Arabs say: "Their dwellings face one another (tatanahar)," meaning: this one is opposite that one, i.e., in front of it. It is also mentioned that some of Banu Asad recited to him:

Abu Hakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujalid,
and the lord of the people of al-Abtah, the one who faces (al-mutanahir)?

[[Report 191: Ibn Kathir also transmitted this (1:53).]]

I.e., one whose throat faces another's throat.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is the view of the one who said: the meaning is: make all your prayer purely for your Lord, to the exclusion of whatever else, of rivals and gods; and likewise make your sacrifice for Him, not for idols, in gratitude to Him for the honour and the good which He has granted you, which has no equal, and which He has singled you out with, namely His giving you al-Kawthar.

I say that this is the most correct of the opinions on this matter because Allah, mighty is His praise, informed His Prophet ﷺ of the honour and dignity with which He had favoured him, and of His bounty upon him in giving him al-Kawthar, and then followed that with His saying ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾. It was thus known that He singled him out for prayer to Him and sacrifice as thanks to Him, for the blessing He had made him aware of in giving him al-Kawthar. There is no basis for restricting part of the prayer, or part of the sacrifice, to this matter, since it is an exhortation to give thanks for blessings.

The meaning of the speech, then, is: Indeed, We have granted you, O Muhammad, al-Kawthar, as a favour from Us upon you and an honour from Us to you. So devote your worship sincerely to your Lord, and single out for Him your prayer and your sacrifice, in contrast to what the one who disbelieves in Him does, who worships other than Him and sacrifices to idols.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾

By His saying, mighty is His praise: ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾ means: indeed, your hater, O Muhammad, and your foe, ﴿is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾. By "al-abtar" is meant: the least and most humiliated, the one whose line is cut off, who has no offspring.

The exegetes differed concerning who is meant by this. Some said: it refers to al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he says: your enemy.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: it is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, who said: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr say: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: it is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hilal, who said: I asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr about His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: your enemy, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, was cut off from his people.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, who said: I am a hater of Muhammad, and whoever is hated by people is the one cut off.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: it is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, who said: I am a hater of Muhammad, and he is cut off, having no offspring. Allah said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. Qatadah said: al-abtar: the lowly, the insignificant, the humiliated.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾: this is al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; it has reached us that he said: I am a hater of Muhammad.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: the man would say: Muhammad is only cut off, he has no offspring as you see, and Allah said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾.

Others said: it refers to ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shimr ibn ʿAtiyyah, who said: ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt used to say: he (the Prophet ﷺ) will have no surviving son, and he is cut off; so Allah revealed these verses concerning him: ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾, ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, ﴿is the one cut off﴾.

Others said: it refers to a group of Quraysh.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, concerning this verse: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in jibt and taghut and say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way"?﴾ He said: it was revealed concerning Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, who came to Mecca, and its people said to him: are we better, or this cut-off one (al-sunbur) cut off from his people? We are the people of pilgrimage, and with us is the place of sacrifice of camels. He said: you are better. So Allah revealed this verse concerning him, and revealed concerning those who said to the Prophet ﷺ what they said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. [[Report 192: This chain has passed as report 185. The text of the report is in Ibn Kathir (1:53), who said after these narrations: "The tafsir previously transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas is more general and comprehensive", meaning report 188.]]

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Badr ibn ʿUthman, from ʿIkrimah ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾, he said: when revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ, Quraysh said: Muhammad has been cut off from us, so it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. He said: the one who calls you cut off is the one cut off.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf came to Mecca, they came to him and said: We are the people of watering and the keeping of the Kaaba, and you are the chief of the people of Medina; are we better, or this cut-off sunbur from his people, who claims he is better than us? He said: rather, you are better than him. So this was revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. He said: and this was revealed to him: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book﴾ ... to His saying ﴿a helper﴾.

The most correct of these views in my opinion is to say: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that the hater of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the least and most humiliated, whose line is cut off. This is the description of everyone among mankind who hates him, even if the verse was revealed concerning a particular individual.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Kawthar.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 108, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar (1), so pray to your Lord and sacrifice (2). Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off (3).﴾

.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿al-Kawthar﴾. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of al-Kawthar. Some of them said: It is a river in Paradise which Allah gave to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold and silver, flowing over pearls and rubies. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Muharib ibn Dithar al-Bahili, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river in Paradise whose banks are gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its water whiter than snow, sweeter than honey, and its soil more fragrant than the scent of musk."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, whose banks are of gold and silver, flowing over rubies and pearls, its water whiter than snow and sweeter than honey."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyya, from Shaqiq or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'isha: "O Mother of the Believers, what is Buttan al-Jannah?" She said: "The middle of Paradise. Its banks are palaces of pearls and rubies, its soil is musk, and its pebbles are pearls and rubies."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Nadr and Shababa narrated to us, both said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from a man, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise; no one puts his two fingers in his ears except that he hears the murmur of that river."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far; and Ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Anas, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, of hollow pearls."

⁕ Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, upon which are vessels equal in number to the stars of the sky."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'isha, who said: "Whoever wishes to hear the murmur of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "A river in Paradise, whose two banks are of hollow pearls."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Mu'adh 'Isa ibn Yazid, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'A'isha, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in the buttan (inner part) of Paradise, the middle of Paradise. In it is a river whose banks are hollow pearls, and in it are vessels for the people of Paradise equal in number to the stars of the sky."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river which Allah gave Muhammad (ﷺ) in Paradise."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Mas'ada narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its soil is pungent musk, and its water is wine."

⁕ Ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A river in Paradise."

⁕ al-Rabi' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Shurayk ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrate to us, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, Jibril took him into the lowest heaven. There he came upon a river, upon which was a palace of pearls and zabarjad (chrysolite). He went to smell its soil, and it was musk. He said: 'O Jibril, what is this river?' He said: 'It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept hidden for you.'"

And others said: What is meant by al-Kawthar is abundant good.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, he said: Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding al-Kawthar: "It is the abundant good which Allah gave him." Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Indeed, people claim that it is a river in Paradise." He said: Sa'id said: "The river in Paradise is part of the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who said: Muharib ibn Dithar said: "What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar?" I said: "He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: It is abundant good." He said: "He spoke the truth, by Allah."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is the abundant good which Allah gave." I said to Sa'id: "We used to hear that it is a river in Paradise." He said: "It is the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Imara ibn Abi Hafsa, from 'Ikrima, who said: "It is prophethood and the good which Allah gave him."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Harmi ibn 'Imara narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, he said: 'Imara informed me, from 'Ikrima, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good, the Qur'an and wisdom."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, he said: 'Imara ibn Abi Hafsa narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, that he said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "Abundant good."

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hilal, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and he said: "Allah multiplied good for him." I said: "A river in Paradise?" He said: "A river and other things."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Mujahid: "Al-Kawthar: all good."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The good of this world and the Hereafter."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding al-Kawthar, who said: "It is abundant good."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Al-Kawthar: abundant good."

⁕ He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Badr ibn 'Uthman, who heard 'Ikrima say regarding al-Kawthar: "What was given to the Prophet of good, prophethood and the Qur'an."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to us, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Badr, from 'Ikrima, his saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "The good which Allah gave: prophethood and Islam."

And others said: It is a pool (hawd) given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Paradise.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mutar, from 'Ata': ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, he said: "A pool in Paradise given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Mutar narrated to us, he said: I asked 'Ata' while we were circumambulating the House, about His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾, and he said: "A pool given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

The most correct of these views in my judgment is the view of the one who said: It is the name of the river which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given in Paradise, and Allah described it as abundant because of its great rank.

We only said that this is the most correct of these views because of the successive reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it is so.

Mention of the reports transmitted regarding that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrate from Qatada, from Anas, who said: "When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was taken up into Paradise, or as he said, there appeared to him a river whose banks are hollow rubies, or he said: hollow (mujawwab). The angel with him struck it with his hand, and drew out musk. Muhammad said to the angel with him: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.' He said: 'The Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and he saw at it a great trace.'" Or as he said.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While I was walking in Paradise, there appeared to me a river whose banks are domes of hollow pearls. The angel with me said: 'Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.' He struck his hand toward its ground and drew out musk from its clay."

⁕ Ibn 'Awf narrated to me, he said: Adam narrated to us, he said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Qatada, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I was taken up to the heaven, I came upon a river whose banks are domes of hollow pearls. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which your Lord gave you.' The angel then swung his hand and drew out its clay as very fragrant musk."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I entered Paradise, and there I was with a river whose banks are tents of pearls. I struck my hand into what flowed in it, and it was very fragrant musk. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is al-Kawthar which Allah gave you.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, he said: Hammam narrated to us, he said: Qatada narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar to the report of Yazid from Sa'id.
